summary: Updates RFC 8410 to clarify existing semantics and add missing ones for the key usage bits in certificates supporting the Ed25519, Ed448, X25519, and X448 elliptic curve algorithms. It is a standards-track specification.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 9295 clarifies which key usage values belong in certificates for Ed25519, Ed448, X25519, and X448 keys. The required and forbidden values depend on the algorithm and, for signing keys, the certificate's role.

subtitle: Clarifies certificate key usage rules for four elliptic-curve algorithms.

tldr.problem: RFC 8410 did not fully define which key usage values are allowed or forbidden for certificates using Ed25519, Ed448, X25519, and X448.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC replaces Section 5 of RFC 8410 with key usage requirements for key-agreement keys and for signing keys in end-entity, CRL issuer, and certification authority certificates.
tldr.outcome: RFC 9295 is a Proposed Standard that updates RFC 8410 with explicit key usage semantics.

facts.label: Required usage for X25519 and X448

today: RFC 9295 is a Proposed Standard from September 2022 and updates RFC 8410.

sections.title: Why the Rules Needed Clarification
sections.content:
RFC 8410 specifies algorithm identifiers for Ed25519, Ed448, X25519, and X448 in certificates. It did not define all forbidden keyUsage values, and it did not refer to keyEncipherment or dataEncipherment.

RFC 9295 replaces Section 5 of RFC 8410 with rules for the intended application of these keys, using the keyUsage certificate extension.
sections.plainLanguage: The earlier rules did not fully say which key usage values were forbidden. This RFC replaces that section with more complete rules.

sections.title: Key-Agreement and Signing Keys
sections.content:
When keyUsage is present for id-X25519 or id-X448, keyAgreement MUST be present. encipherOnly and decipherOnly may also be present. Digital-signature, encipherment, and certificate-signing values listed in the RFC MUST NOT be present.

For id-Ed25519 or id-Ed448, the required values depend on certificate role. An end-entity certificate must contain at least one of nonRepudiation, digitalSignature, or cRLSign. A CRL issuer certificate must contain cRLSign; a certification authority certificate must contain keyCertSign. The RFC also specifies which other values are forbidden for each role.
sections.plainLanguage: X25519 and X448 certificates with keyUsage must include keyAgreement. Ed25519 and Ed448 certificates follow different requirements depending on whether they are end-entity, CRL issuer, or certification authority certificates.

sections.title: Security and IANA
sections.content: The document introduces no new security considerations beyond those in RFC 8410. It has no IANA actions.
sections.plainLanguage: The update adds no new security considerations and requires no IANA changes.
